subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: What framework-level plugin circuit breaker contract should OpenClaw support for hook/tool execution, persisted state, operator controls, and default degradation behavior?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but choosing storage schema, fail modes, forced-open behavior, status/reset surfaces, and default-on policy changes plugin runtime and third-party plugin contracts.

options.title: Design core breaker contract first
options.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, metrics/status/reset surfaces, compatibility mode, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

options.title: Keep breakers plugin-local
options.body: Continue the Active Memory pattern and only add narrow SDK helpers if multiple plugins need shared breaker mechanics.

options.title: Start with passive telemetry
options.body: Add attribution and log-only evaluation first, then decide active open/half-open behavior after deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker contract first
recommendation.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, metrics/status/reset surfaces, compatibility mode, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface history across hook timeouts, plugin-state storage, and session-lock hardening.
